title: Optimized Nonlinear Grey Bernoulli Model for Nowcasting the Philippine Gross Domestic Product
venue: European Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics
tldr: PSO-optimized Nonlinear Grey Bernoulli Model achieved 5.45% out-of-sample MAPE for Philippine GDP nowcasting, outperforming standard grey model benchmarks.
problem_and_motivation: Accurate and timely GDP forecasts are essential for economic policymaking, but official statistics are released quarterly with delays of up to two months. The NGBM(1,1) model can capture complex patterns but its performance depends heavily on precise estimation of parameters.
approach: Quarterly Philippine GDP data from Q1 2021 to Q4 2024 sourced from the Philippine Statistics Authority OpenSTAT portal.
NGBM(1,1) model optimized using Particle Swarm Optimization with 40-particle swarm and 1000 max iterations.
Alternative exponential background value method following Cheng et al.
Harmonic function simulation with 15 parameter combinations evaluated under 70/30 and 80/20 splits.
Benchmarked against standard GM(1,1), traditional NGBM(1,1), and Exponential NGBM(1,1).
Post-modeling seasonal decomposition applied to address systematic Q4 prediction errors.
findings: num: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieved the lowest out-of-sample MAPE of 5.45%, outperforming Exponential NGBM(1,1) at 5.76%, GM(1,1) at 5.77%, and NGBM(1,1) at 5.87%.
num: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieved the lowest out-of-sample RMSE of 362,077.8.
num: After seasonal adjustment, all models achieved MAPE below 1%, with PSO-NGBM(1,1) at 0.38%.
num: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieved a near-perfect prediction in 2024 Q2 with a prediction error of 0.0001%.
PSO algorithm converged to near-optimal solution within approximately 30 iterations.
Prediction errors peaked during Q4 across all models, indicating unmodeled seasonal patterns.

key_equations.explanation: Out-of-sample Mean Absolute Percentage Error used as the fitness function.
NGBM(1,1) whitening equation incorporating the Bernoulli power index m.
Harmonic regression model used in the simulation study.

definitions.definition: Nonlinear Grey Bernoulli Model, a first-order grey model extended with a Bernoulli differential equation.
Particle Swarm Optimization, a metaheuristic algorithm inspired by collective behavior of bird flocks.
Accumulated Generating Operation, a cumulative sum transformation that smoothens raw data sequences.
Mean Absolute Percentage Error, a metric measuring forecast accuracy as a percentage.
Root Mean Square Error, a metric measuring average magnitude of forecast errors.
Gross Domestic Product, the total monetary value of all finished goods and services produced within a country.
Prediction of the present, very near future, or very recent past, particularly for economic indicators released with delay.

topics.name: Forecasting Algorithms for Sequential Spending Data
topics.justification: Evaluates NGBM(1,1) and its variants for sequential quarterly economic data forecasting with small sample sizes.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Advances the application of grey forecasting models to macroeconomic nowcasting by demonstrating that Particle Swarm Optimization substantially improves parameter estimation of NGBM(1,1). Introduces a systematic simulation-based approach for selecting optimal data-splitting schemes.
directly_justifies: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieved the lowest out-of-sample MAPE of 5.45% for Philippine GDP nowcasting.
Seasonal adjustment reduced forecast MAPE from over 5% to below 1%.
The 70/30 training-to-testing split provided marginally superior forecasting accuracy in 8 of 15 scenarios.
PSO optimization converged within approximately 30 iterations.
limits: Only 16 quarterly observations available, constraining dataset size.
All grey models failed to capture seasonal dynamics without explicit preprocessing.
No formal statistical significance testing conducted.
Study is limited to Philippine GDP data.

limitations: Only 16 quarterly observations were available, constraining dataset size and potentially limiting generalizability.
All grey models failed to capture seasonal dynamics without explicit preprocessing.
No formal statistical significance testing was conducted to validate differences in model performance.
The study is limited to Philippine GDP data and does not test on other economic indicators or countries.
The exponential background value optimization yielded minimal gains.
remember_this: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieved the lowest out-of-sample MAPE of 5.45% for Philippine GDP nowcasting.
Seasonal adjustment reduced MAPE from over 5% to below 1% across all grey model variants.
PSO converged within approximately 30 iterations, indicating efficient parameter optimization.
A 70/30 training-to-testing split was marginally superior to 80/20 for grey model performance.
All grey models struggled with Q4 prediction errors due to unmodeled seasonal patterns.
